name: Hyphon Events Manager
author: hyphonsports

sections.description:
Hyphon Events Manager provides event and performance management, ticket pricing,
WooCommerce checkout, digital QR tickets and entrance scanning from WordPress.

The WordPress.org plugin is a complete, permanently functional event-management
and general-admission ticketing plugin. It includes calendars, calendar filters
and feeds, recurring-event tools, coupons, QR tickets and browser scanning.

Optional separately installed Hyphon extensions can add allocated seating,
managed scanner devices and guest-list workflows. Their implementation is not
included in this WordPress.org plugin and no included feature requires a trial,
licence key or remote activation.

WooCommerce is required for online ticket payments. Venues retain control of
their WooCommerce payment providers.

External services

Hyphon Events sends ticket purchases to the WooCommerce installation on the
same website. WooCommerce and any payment gateway selected by the site owner
may communicate with their own services under their respective terms and
privacy policies. Hyphon Events itself does not send visitor, order or ticket
data to a Hyphon licensing or analytics service.

If the site owner enables the optional Facebook video feed and enters a
Facebook Page identifier and access token, Hyphon Events requests that Page’s
published video list from the Meta Graph API so it can display those videos on
the website. The request sends the configured Page identifier, requested video
fields, result limit and access token. No ticket-buyer, order or visitor data
is sent. The request occurs only after the site owner configures and enables
this feature. Meta’s Terms are at https://www.facebook.com/terms.php and its
Privacy Policy is at https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/.

Development source

All JavaScript and CSS shipped with the plugin is human-readable source and can
be edited directly. There is no compilation or minification step for these
assets.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Upload and activate Hyphon Events Manager.
  3. Open Event Manager in WordPress administration.
  4. Create ticket prices, an event and its performances.
  5. Add the supplied event-list shortcode to the venue’s events page.
sections.faq:
Does Hyphon Events process the venue’s ticket income?

No. Ticket payments are processed through WooCommerce and the payment gateways
configured by the venue.

Do included features require a licence or trial?

No. Every feature and line of implementation included in the WordPress.org ZIP
remains available without a licence key or time limit.

0.20.15

  • Updated the built-in Hyphon Events branding artwork.

0.20.14

  • Scoped administration assets to Hyphon screens, removed a release marker file and tightened output escaping for WordPress.org review.

0.20.11

  • Removed ticket-bundle implementation from the WordPress.org Free package rather than shipping inaccessible controls.
  • Added nonce and object-level permission checks to event edit, save and delete routes.
  • Documented the optional Meta Graph API video-feed connection, the data sent and when it is used.
  • Added release checks that reject paid bundle implementation in the Free ZIP.

0.20.10

  • Moved interface CSS and JavaScript into WordPress-enqueued, human-readable assets.
  • Routed server-generated script configuration through WordPress inline-script APIs.
  • Added release checks that reject direct executable script and style blocks in the WordPress.org ZIP.
  • Kept all Free calendar features enabled when moving between Free, Plus and Pro packages.
  • Fixed the public My Account navigation URL in WordPress.org builds and subdirectory installations.
  • Resolved duplicate coupon codes against the correct event and preserved the selected coupon usage record.
  • Kept the event booking panel fully inside narrow mobile viewports.
  • Aligned full-width event pages correctly inside padded mobile themes.
  • Re-audited permissions, nonces, escaping and clean-install compatibility.

0.20.4

  • Separated the WordPress.org build completely from the Freemius SDK and licence checks.
  • Made included calendar filters, feeds, recurring-event and display tools permanently available in Free.
  • Added release checks preventing paid implementation or licensing code entering the Free ZIP.
  • Moved the top-level Events menu to the standard content-management area.
  • Clarified external-service use and the editable source format of bundled assets.

0.20.3

  • Fixed event pages stripping their generated booking form, scripts and styles under standard WordPress theme rendering.
  • Restored interactive ticket quantities, allocated seating, coupon controls and checkout submission on fresh installations.

0.18.9

  • Preserve each WooCommerce order’s original currency in My Tickets and reports when a store later changes its default currency.
  • Keep mixed-currency revenue totals separate instead of combining unlike currencies.

0.18.8

  • Use the WooCommerce store currency throughout public booking, coupons, administration and checkout totals.

0.18.7

  • Fixed My Tickets account matching so paid bookings are recovered securely by the signed-in customer’s email as well as the stored account link.

0.18.6

  • Finalised the Free, Plus and Pro package boundaries for Freemius distribution.
  • Kept paid-only ticketing, scanner-device and guest-list implementation out of the Free package.
  • Preserved events, performances, WooCommerce orders and reusable configuration when changing editions.
  • Verified authenticated automatic updates through the released Freemius deployment.

0.18.5

  • Added fail-closed edition loading and strengthened package-boundary checks.

0.18.4

  • Completed Freemius licensing, plan recognition and update integration.

0.18.0

  • Added the release-ready Free, Plus and Pro commercial structure.
  • Added a WordPress administration comparison screen for edition features.

0.16.12

  • Separate performance and ticket-selection steps more clearly.
  • Keep public seating-plan rows level when aisle widths vary.

0.16.11

  • Match performance-time typography to the public Hyphon Events interface.

0.16.10

  • Removed the duplicate Twenty Twenty-Five featured image from Hyphon event detail pages, leaving one branded hero image.

0.16.9

  • Removed duplicate Twenty Twenty-Five page-title headings from the demo, scanner and My Account application pages.

0.16.8

  • Replaced the Twenty Twenty-Five Manrope/serif mixture with one consistent Arial/Helvetica system font stack across the public site and Hyphon interfaces.

0.16.7

  • Corrected the Twenty Twenty-Five template selectors so the complete demo card system receives the Hyphon visual treatment.

0.16.6

  • Aligned the demo landing page, event cards and booking actions with the My Tickets navy, gold, burgundy and cream visual system.
  • Added consistent card borders, typography, buttons, spacing, shadows and mobile treatment.

0.16.5

  • Prevented the retired ticket-sales endpoint and upgrade helper from recreating performance-level copies of global ticket and seating plan data.
  • Increased mobile seating controls for clearer, safer touch interaction while retaining horizontal seat-map scrolling.

0.16.4

  • Removed the remaining event-save, duplication and legacy meta-box paths that could copy global ticket or seating plans onto performances.

0.16.3

  • Added canonical global ticket-plan and seating-plan resolution without copied performance metadata.
  • Corrected event deletion, shortcode rendering, theme-page compatibility and public white-labelling.
  • Added a dedicated least-privilege ticket-scanner capability for door staff.
  • Improved the event-first dashboard, attendance, reporting, guest-list and WooCommerce workflows.
  • Preserved existing WooCommerce orders, payments, tickets and legitimate event data during upgrades.

0.11.9

  • Added event-specific offline ticket downloads for authorised Pro scanners.
  • Added idempotent offline-admission synchronisation and duplicate reconciliation.
  • Added a per-device Offline entry control.

0.11.8

  • Corrected event and performance edit buttons in the event-first dashboard.

0.11.7

  • Added a seven-day operational licence grace period for already-paired scanners.
  • Kept new scanner pairing restricted to a currently confirmed Pro installation.
  • Added scanner licence state to the public scanner protocol responses.
  • Preserved immediate remote logout by rotating the individual device token.
  • Added the event-first tickets dashboard and event-scoped arrivals export.

0.11.6

  • Added event-first ticket administration with event totals, ticket breakdowns and arrivals.
  • Simplified the main ticket navigation around events, arrivals, scanning and seating.

0.11.4

  • Fix scanner login QR rendering on the Scanner Devices screen.

0.11.3

  • Prevent scanner check-in across different events.
  • Add one-time website login QR codes for scanner pairing.
  • Add QR login scanning and branded header to the Android scanner.

0.11.2

  • Added an isolated internal plan tester for switching between Free, Plus and Pro.
  • Kept the tester out of all customer release packages.

0.11.1

  • Restored the Free, Plus and Pro commercial structure.
  • Added plan-aware Freemius entitlement and a three-column feature comparison.
  • Assigned enhanced ticket sales to Plus and entrance operations to Pro.

0.11.0

  • Added the Freemius-ready licensing and update adapter.
  • Added a licence and update status area to Free & Pro administration.
  • Added a staged commercial-release plan without changing event-ticket payments.

0.10.4

  • Completed generic Hyphon booking URLs with backwards compatibility.
  • Corrected QR payload prefix parsing.
